To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the failure of hierarchically structured bundles of fibres is governed by a universal law and that this law is independent of the specific properties of an individual fiber and of the specific organization of the hierarchy.
for any hierarchical organization the failure properties of a bundle are determined by the number of fibres in the smallest bundles and the number of these smallest bundles.

the threshold for the failure of a fibre-bundle obeys a universal power law with respect to its size, that this law is preserved for hierarchically organized fibre-bundles, and that the exponent is independent of the details of the failure properties of the fibres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the failure properties of an ensemble of fibres depend on the organization of these fibres in bundles.
the question of how failure of a system of interacting elements depends on the structure of the system and the failure properties of its elements.
the scaling of failure of hierarchically arranged fibre bundles and its implications for the failure of materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of any information on the failure properties of an elementary fibre, the failure of a fibre system with a hierarchical structure is determined by its total size.
the failure of a hierarchical fibre bundle is not a hierarchical phenomenon but a phenomenon of a bundle of a given size, independent of its position in the hierarchy.
the scaling law is the most general property of the failure of hierarchical distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scaling law for failure of fibre bundles is universal with respect to the failure properties of individual fibres and the hierarchical organization.
the scaling laws are universal, whereas the failure thresholds are non-universal.
, in contrast to what is often assumed, the failure properties of a bundle of fibres are independent of their hierarchical organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to the common belief, the failure properties of a bundle are not determined by the failure properties of the individual fibres, but by the hierarchical organization of the fibres.
the failure properties of hierarchical fibre bundles are governed by universal properties of the underlying failure mechanism.
the failure of hierarchical fibre bundles does not obey the same universal laws that are observed for homogeneous fibre bundles.
